audit_findings.title: The valuation uses a pre-acquisition balance sheet and earnings base for post-acquisition common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed $1.4 billion purchase price and $1.6 billion new borrowings; borrowings equal 40.9% of the computed $3.913 billion base equity value; net value effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds pre-close cash and shows only pre-close debt, while equity-level OE excludes both PSS earnings and post-close interest expense.
audit_findings.evidence: The acquisition was funded through a combination of cash on hand, $ 800 million of borrowings under the Company’s $ 1.0 billion credit agreement, and proceeds from the $ 800 million private placement of senior notes described below.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated: the acquisition closed August 3, before the September 6 valuation, but the valuation describes the July 31 company. Missing PSS earnings could understate value, while retained pre-close cash and omitted financing costs could overstate it. The transaction's scale is plainly capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Rerun on one synchronized post-closing date using actual cash, debt, fees, interest expense, PSS owner earnings and fully diluted shares.

audit_findings.title: Material acquired liabilities ahead of common equity remain unidentified
audit_findings.mechanism: Assumed liabilities either reduce the equity bridge directly or reduce combined-company OE through recurring cash costs.
audit_findings.evidence: Due to the proximity of the acquisition date to the issuance date of these consolidated financial statements, the Company has not completed the valuation of the assets acquired and liabilities assumed and is therefore unable to disclose the preliminary purchase price allocation, including the amounts assigned to the major classes of assets acquired, liabilities assumed, goodwill, or the supplemental unaudited pro forma information.
audit_findings.explanation: The absence of a purchase-price allocation is demonstrated, but the amount and nature of the assumed liabilities are not. Because the $1.4 billion acquisition is material, omitted claims may affect value, but the current record cannot establish their magnitude.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the first post-close 10-Q and purchase-price allocation; map every assumed liability to either a bridge deduction or a recurring cost retained in OE.

audit_findings.title: Purging investment income may break the deferred-compensation offset
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed investment and other income was $5.628 million and deferred-compensation assets and liabilities were each $22.019 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Removing asset-side investment gains while retaining matching liability remeasurement expense would depress historical OE and the fitted anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: The increase in investment and other income in fiscal 2026 was primarily due to an increase in the market value of securities held in deferred compensation plans.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates matching deferred-compensation assets and liabilities and identifies securities appreciation as the primary reason investment income increased. It does not demonstrate which income components were purged or whether the offsetting expense remained, so the error and its materiality remain unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Trace the FY2026 investment-income purge and corresponding deferred-compensation expense account by account, then rerun with both sides retained or both removed.

audit_findings.title: Treatment of the $35.7 million PSS transaction charge is not demonstrated
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed $35.7 million pre-tax charge, equal to 15.0% of the $237.5 million anchor OE; resulting anchor effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Retention depresses FY2026 OE and the trend anchor; an indiscriminate add-back could omit continuing integration, retention, systems or restructuring cash costs.
audit_findings.evidence: The increase in operating income in fiscal 2026 was primarily due to organic sales growth in both reportable segments, gross margin improvements across both reportable segments, and SG&A cost efficiencies in the Europe & Australia segment, partially offset by PSS transaction-related costs of $35.7 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The charge is large relative to anchor OE, but the record does not show whether it was retained, added back or separated by economic character. Either treatment could materially distort value, and the direction cannot be established without the OE bridge and prospective cost evidence.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the FY2026 OE bridge, identify any add-back, separate completed transaction fees from continuing cash integration costs, and rerun the historical anchor and forward OE consistently.

audit_findings.title: A discrete tax benefit may remain in the earnings base
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed $6.137 million, 2.6% of the $237.5 million anchor; a conservative dollar-for-dollar base-anchor sensitivity is approximately $1.99 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: If retained, the nonrecurring tax benefit raises FY2026 OE and slightly raises the ten-year fitted anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: During the year ended July 31, 2026 , the Company recognized $ 6,137 of tax benefits (including interest and penalties) associated with the lapse of statutes of limitations.
audit_findings.explanation: Treatment is not demonstrated, but scale is insufficient to alter the conclusion. Even assuming the entire benefit flowed directly into the anchor—more impact than a ten-year trend fit would ordinarily transmit—the computed base value would move by about $1.99 per share, versus the $9.25 gap between the $80.96 base value and $90.21 market price and the $24.29 gap to the $56.67 buy-below price.
audit_findings.action: Confirm normalization of the $6.137 million benefit and apply the same treatment to comparable historical tax releases; no full valuation rerun is required unless broader tax-normalization inconsistencies are found.

audit_findings.title: The denominator blends two common classes with unequal economic preferences
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed annual Class A preference of $0.01665 per share; approximately $0.722 million across 43.361 million outstanding Class A shares, or 0.018% of the $3.913 billion base equity value; computed Class A adjustment is about $0.012 per share using a 10% perpetuity and the diluted class mix
audit_findings.mechanism: Dividing aggregate common value by combined diluted shares assigns part of the Class A dividend preference to Class B and therefore slightly understates BRC Class A value.
audit_findings.evidence: Before any dividend may be paid on the Class B Common Stock, holders of the Class A Common Stock are entitled to receive an annual, noncumulative cash dividend of $ 0.01665 per share.
audit_findings.explanation: The blended denominator is technically imprecise, but the contractual preference is negligible relative to both aggregate equity value and the $80.96 base value per share. The liquidation preference also does not meaningfully affect a going-concern valuation at the stated equity value.
audit_findings.action: If Class A-specific precision is desired, capitalize and allocate the Class A preference before dividing the residual value between classes; otherwise retain the blended result with disclosure.
